item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q017_prp8_evolutionary_mosaic","answer":"In current SCOPe release 2.08, Prp8 is chain A of the 3.6-Å Schizosaccharomyces pombe spliceosome structure 3jb9 and is divided into five classified domains. Four reuse previously observed domain architectures: residues 698–822 (d3jb9a4; a.29.2.1) belong to the bromodomain family; residues 823–1604 (d3jb9a3; e.8.1.8) are the Prp8 reverse-transcriptase domain within the DNA/RNA-polymerase superfamily e.8.1; residues 1605–1780 (d3jb9a2; c.52.1.36) are a Prp8 endonuclease-like family within the restriction-endonuclease-like superfamily c.52.1; and residues 1784–2030 (d3jb9a1; c.55.3.14) form the Prp8 beta-finger family within the RNase-H-like superfamily c.55.3. The large N-terminal domain, residues 47–697 (d3jb9a5; d.394.1.1), defines the distinct N-terminal Prp8 fold d.394 and is the newly observed fold.\n\nThis mixture supports an evolutionary-mosaic history: Prp8 was assembled by accretion or extreme divergence of modules related to bromodomains, polymerases/reverse transcriptases, restriction endonucleases, and RNase H, together with a structurally novel N-terminal module. The RT–endonuclease–RNase-H combination is consistent with, but does not alone prove, ancestry involving group-II-intron/retroelement machinery. Evolutionary strength must be kept distinct: the bromodomain assignment is at family level, whereas the RT, endonuclease-like, and RNase-H-like connections to other characterized proteins are principally superfamily-level remote relationships; sharing only a fold would be weaker and would not by itself establish homology. These classifications do not demonstrate retained polymerase, nuclease, RNase-H, histone-binding, or other functions, so such activities must not be transferred without independent biochemical evidence. Likewise, templates should be selected domain-by-domain rather than treating this mosaic chain as one homologous unit. Chain 3jb9A is its own release-specific chain-cluster representative, but that status is not evidence that it is the optimal structural template; the five classified intervals also cover only part of the 2,363-residue chain.","evidence_used":["/api/v1","/api/v1/openapi.yaml","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/3jb9","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/3jb9/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a3","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a4","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a5","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Prp8&limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a2/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a3/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a4/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a5/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a1/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a2/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a3/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a4/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a5/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a1/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a2/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a3/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a4/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3jb9a5/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/chains/3jb9A"]}]}
